root_idea.summary: The root centers on forcefully turning an opponent away while bringing him low: repulsion joined to abasement.
root_idea.development: The lexical range extends from throwing someone down or prostrate to repelling, routing, thwarting, and humiliating an opponent; related formations also preserve associations with the liver and with inward rage or grief.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form كَبَتَ rather than the QAC passive lemma كُبِتَ.

senses.definition: To forcefully repel or suppress an opponent, overcoming and humiliating him.
senses.usage_conditions: The active Quranic use presents an opponent as suppressed; the passive uses present opponents as overcome and disgraced. The voice difference is grammatical rather than a separate lexical meaning.

A reported alternative interpretation of the Quranic passive expression understands the state described as rage and grief rather than abasement through defeat. The historical citation associated with this interpretation is not assigned a modern verse location here.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To throw someone or something down prostrate, or onto the face.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form I use; the physical act is also used in a curse or imprecation wishing that someone be brought low.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To repel or turn away an opponent, rout him, and frustrate or abase him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classical active constructions may describe repelling an enemy in anger, putting him to flight, denying him his desired outcome, or causing him to fail to attain it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be thrown down prostrate or to fall prostrate, including onto the face.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form VII intransitive or passive-like use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To smite or hurt the liver.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical or idiomatic use equated with كَبَدَ.
Variant nominal forms identified with كَبِدٌ; the liver is also used idiomatically in expressions about rage or its abatement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rage or wrath; grief or sorrow.
Affected with violent grief or sorrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial formation; the entry also identifies it as the passive participle of كَبَتَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Filled with grief or sorrow, or with rage or wrath.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active-participial or adjectival description of an emotionally overwhelmed person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To restrain one's rage within oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional construction describing the containment of anger in the inner self or bosom.

cautions: The public headword is normalized to the active Form I perfect كَبَتَ, while the supplied QAC lemma is the passive form كُبِتَ.
The reported rage-and-grief interpretation is preserved, but the historical citation associated with it is not converted into a modern verse location.
